header: Date: 2026-10-01 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Sofia Patel, Miguel Ortega (Redwood) — Claire Simmons, Derek Huang, Priya Rao (NimbleHealth)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on access gating, staging inference performance, and next steps for security and networking. NimbleHealth reported intermittent high tail latency on 99th percentile during burst traffic; Redwood SE proposed batch/quant tradeoffs and KV cache tuning. Action items: share security artifacts, re-run targeted throughput test, schedule maintenance window for VPC peering, and upload prompt traces for evals.
topics: Onboarding progress and remaining access blockers
KV cache and prefix caching behavior
Quantization profile and batch size tradeoffs
VPC peering and firewall egress configuration
transcript:
00:00:00 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:00:05 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Hi, Claire here.
00:00:07 Speaker: Derek Huang — Derek from infra.
00:00:09 Speaker: Priya Rao — Priya, ML.
00:00:12 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Miguel, SE, Redwood.
00:00:15 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Awesome. Agenda: access gating, current bench results, and next steps. Claire, do you want to start with the status on credentials?
00:00:28 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Yeah, quick update: we have the staging service account but the VPC peering hasn't been scheduled, we hit a backlog in change window. So currently traffic is going via our nat gateway which adds some jitter.
00:00:45 Speaker: Derek Huang — to add, we've locked down egress to only approved IP ranges, but the list we gave earlier needs to be adjusted to add the redwood cluster range. I can do that this week if we get the ranges.
00:01:01 Speaker: Sofia Patel — OK, we sent that cluster CIDR in the last email but i'll reattach. Miguel — any blocker on our side for the peering?
00:01:12 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — No blocker, we just need the exact prefix and a time window to avoid rolling deploys overlapping. Also note we can do a temporary ssh tunnel / bastion for debug but won't be ideal for steady-state traffic.
00:01:29 Speaker: Priya Rao — for the bench tests, we saw 95th percentile around 180ms but 99th was at 1.2s during a 200 req/s burst. That's what worries product folks.
00:01:44 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Right, that aligns with KV cold misses. Our runtime does automatic prefix caching but if prompt prefixes vary a lot you hit more KV lookups. Two levers: increase KV cache TTL and tune batching.
00:02:00 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Can you explain KV cache TTL in plain terms? We had an ops person ask what gets cached.
00:02:07 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Sure. When a conversation reuses a prefix or recent tokens, the runtime keeps key/value states so next request avoids recomputing the entire context. TTL here is how long we keep those entries before eviction. If TTL is low, more cold-starts => tail latency. But memory usage increases with higher TTL.
00:02:30 Speaker: Priya Rao — Memory isn't our bottleneck right now, infra says we've got room for larger caches in staging.
00:02:37 Speaker: Derek Huang — correct, staging has margin but production plans will be different. We want to understand cost impact if TTL goes up.
00:02:46 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Miguel, could you outline the recommended TTL and batch size changes to test?
00:02:52 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — For this workload, try TTL=600s for the first run and batch size from 4 to 8. Also test quant profile q4 (INT4-like) vs q8 to see CPU/GPU tradeoffs. We'll expect lower latency for small seq lengths with q4 but watch for a small drop in quality.
00:03:12 Speaker: Priya Rao — Quality drop: how measurable is that? We have a prompt set of ~250 samples with expected outputs.
00:03:20 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Great — upload those prompts and we'll run automated evals. We'll measure exact-match and a small manual spot-check for hallucination. For the 250 set we can run a baseline and then compare q4 vs q8.
00:03:34 Speaker: Claire Simmons — We'll upload today. One more Q: are we likely to see 99th latency improvements with just TTL and batching or do we need routing/fallbacks?
00:03:45 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — TTL + batching should reduce KV cold miss incidence and lower tail, but for extreme bursts we recommend a small reserved concurrency pool (dedicated lanes) or fallback to a smaller model variant during spike. That tradeoff reduces cost by default but buys predictability.
00:04:01 Speaker: Derek Huang — How fast is fallback switching? Our engineers want automatic sub-second fallback.
00:04:08 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — We can configure policy-based routing with thresholds that trigger a model switch in ~300-500ms, depending on pipeline flushing. That's not instantaneous but we can tune it.
00:04:18 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Let's capture that as an action to test automatic fallback in the lab.
00:04:22 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Sounds good.
00:04:25 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — On security, we had a request for KMS integration and audit logs; Sofia, do we have the updated doc?
00:04:32 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Yes, i'll re-share the security deck. We support customer KMS and can forward key usage logs into your SIEM. Audit logs are available at token and model call level — retention is configurable.
00:04:47 Speaker: Priya Rao — Are the audit logs PII redacted?
00:04:50 Speaker: Sofia Patel — By default we don't store user prompt text in plaintext in audit logs unless enabled; there's a redact pipeline. If you need full prompt retention for evals, we can enable encrypted storage with KMS.
00:05:03 Speaker: Priya Rao — We'll probably need that for debug but only for a subset. We'll document which prompts to retain.
00:05:10 Speaker: Derek Huang — Network-wise, i forwarded the firewall template earlier. One issue: aws nat gateway metrics show occasional spikes during concurrent egress. If peering goes through, we'll remove that choke point.
00:05:23 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — That will likely lower jitter. Also consider routing via regional Redwood nodes to minimize cross-AZ hops.
00:05:31 Speaker: Claire Simmons — ok so next on the bench results — Priya, can you walk through the intermittent failure you saw?
00:05:38 Speaker: Priya Rao — Sure. On three runs we saw 5 dropped responses around 10 minutes into a 30-minute soak. The logs showed an out-of-memory on the worker host then it recovered. I suspect a pattern where a large prompt causes a mem spike and evicts KV entries.
00:05:58 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — That points to long-tail prompt length variation. Two mitigations: enforce max token length at the gateway or increase memory headroom per worker. Also zippering requests (circuit-breaker) to avoid cascading OOMs.
00:06:15 Speaker: Derek Huang — We can add a hard cap at the gateway, but product might not like truncated prompts without fallback messaging.
00:06:23 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Product is okay with a graceful error that explains truncation and asks user to rephrase.
00:06:29 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Good compromise. We'll add that to the gate config.
00:06:33 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — I'll prepare a sample gateway policy.
00:06:36 Speaker: Priya Rao — On quantization: we saw a small shift in answer style with q4 on 12% of samples, mostly more concise replies. Not sure if that's unacceptable.
00:06:48 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — We can tune the decoding temperature and prompt templates to reduce style drift. Also, if it's semantic quality loss, we can keep a small ensemble; route sensitive prompts to q8.
00:06:59 Speaker: Claire Simmons — How do we classify 'sensitive' automatically?
00:07:02 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Could do a simple classifier or use metadata tags from your app. For the POC, manual tagging is fine.
00:07:09 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Action: Priya upload the 250 prompts and tag ~30 as 'sensitive' so we can test routing.
00:07:16 Speaker: Priya Rao — Will do.
00:07:18 Speaker: Derek Huang — About costs: if we increase TTL and memory we'll see higher unit cost per token?
00:07:23 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Slightly higher because more GPU memory and cache hits increase memory footprint, but tokens/sec improves so net cost per request can go down. We'll run a cost model once we have throughput numbers.
00:07:35 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Can Redwood provide a rough cost delta for TTL=600 vs TTL=120?
00:07:40 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Yes, i'll include cost delta in the test results. Expect ~5-12% increase in memory costs but potential 10-25% reduction in tail-induced retries depending on workload.
00:07:54 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Ok, timeline: Miguel will run the test, Derek will open the peering window, Priya uploads prompts, Sofia shares security docs. Any other blockers?
00:08:07 Speaker: Priya Rao — One ask: can we enable higher telemetry retention for 48 hours while we debug?
00:08:12 Speaker: Sofia Patel — We can extend retention for the pilot. We'll enable a 48-hour window for detailed logs.
00:08:18 Speaker: Derek Huang — We'll need to budget for S3 storage, but it's small for 48 hours.
00:08:23 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Fine.
00:08:26 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Quick note: we'll instrument a synthetic trace that hits the worst-case prompts at ramp to reproduce the 99p spike. That will help isolate if it's network or runtime.
00:08:36 Speaker: Priya Rao — Great, add me to that run.
00:08:40 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Will do.
00:08:42 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Any legal/procurement asks this week?
00:08:45 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Not yet. We may request a DPA addendum later but not blocking now.
00:08:51 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Cool. Last: can we confirm dates? I'll send a proposed calendar for the peering maintenance (Derek to pick a slot) and Miguel will deliver benchmark CSV by Monday 10/06.
00:09:03 Speaker: Derek Huang — I'll aim for 10/05 window.
00:09:06 Speaker: Sofia Patel — Perfect. Quick recap: action items noted, we'll follow up in email. Thanks everyone.
00:09:16 Speaker: Claire Simmons — Thanks.
00:09:18 Speaker: Priya Rao — Thanks, bye.
00:09:20 Speaker: Miguel Ortega — Thanks, bye.
00:09:22 Speaker: Sofia Patel — End call.
00:09:24 Note: meeting duration recorded as 46 minutes; timestamps above show selected speaking segments and rough cadence — fuller transcript retained in Fireflies system.
